request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 0 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means results are clear-cut and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means the top configs are too close to call or something looks off. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run to assess consistency. A config that wins consistently across folds is more trustworthy than one with high variance. (Independent run 1, no feature agent.)

concerns: Run 1 (LightGBM) beats the simplest model, run 4 (logistic), by 0.0399 PR-AUC, which is less than one SD (about 0.056-0.064). Under the simplicity rule, logistic is the pick.

Run 1 beats run 4 in 4 of 5 folds. The gap is small in folds 4 and 5 (+0.026 and +0.005 in fold 4 and 5 respectively, fold 4 favours run 4 by -0.024 in fold 4). Overall the edge is consistent in sign but not decisive.
With only 5 folds, 5,410 providers and about 506 positives, fold-to-fold variance is high. Fold PR-AUC ranges from 0.62 to 0.80, so the differences between configurations are within noise.

The PotentialFraud label has an undocumented origin and is only a proxy for suspicion. A ROC-AUC of about 0.94 across all models, including logistic, suggests the label may be largely driven by easily separable features such as provider size or volume, or may come from a rule-based process. This could be a leakage or label-circularity risk, so results may reflect reproducing the label rule rather than detecting fraud.

The no_size feature set only lowers PR-AUC slightly (run 2 vs run 1, confounded with other changes), which suggests size is not the sole driver, but the comparison is confounded by differing imbalance handling and hyperparameters.
The claims window of about 13 months is short and the cross-validation scheme is not documented (random vs temporal). If it is random, performance may be optimistic.
Only 4 configurations were tried, with no tuning of the logistic regression or random forest, and no search rounds remain.
Precision@50 is 0.756 for logistic vs 0.784 for LightGBM, which is a small difference of about 1-2 providers out of 50. The audit queue is 100, so precision at 100 was not reported.
